label: 0053 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 53 windows): 0052 with the total coupling capped at 1 in every window, afterslip periods included, uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, fourteen slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0052 with the total coupling (background plus every afterslip state and slow slip episode, measured along the plate motion) capped at 1 in every window, afterslip periods included, on the Nankai, Japan Trench and Sagami megathrusts. The cap binds off Miyagi at 0–15 km from 2014, over 8,000–11,000 km², and coupling there at 0–20 km averages 0.86 in 2012–2021 (0052: 1.44). The dip-slip coupling shown can still reach about 1.06 where the strike-slip coupling is below 1. Seafloor residuals beneath the Japan Trench after Tohoku are 37 and 71 mm (0052: 28 and 49), and from 2013 to 2021 the sites near the trench still move about 34 mm/yr further landward than the model. Held-out seafloor sites are predicted little better than without the seafloor-driven trench state (+109, against +916 for 0052). Onshore window cross-validation is 235 lower than for 0052, all of it in the Boso slow slip windows, where the cap also limits the episodes' free strike-slip; elsewhere the two match. So the seafloor prefers coupling above 1 off Miyagi after Tohoku. Seafloor data: Japan Coast Guard (CC BY-NC 4.0) and Tohoku University (CC BY 4.0).
